key_insight: On ARC-AGI-1, both pretraining and test-time training budgets materially change model performance, so architecture comparisons between VARC and TRM must be interpreted through the lens of matched training budgets.
engineering_relevance: For engineering teams building few-shot reasoning systems, the study shows that optimizing pretraining and test-time adaptation budgets can matter as much as model design when chasing ARC gains.
method: Crossed 5 pretraining budgets with 4 test-time training (TTT) budgets per test task.
Evaluated VARC and TRM under the same inductive protocol on ARC-AGI-1.
Tracked task-variant count and total sample presentations as controlled budget variables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that increasing TTT sample presentations improves pass@2 for both models, while more task variants consistently help TRM but often hurt or fail to help VARC.
watch_item: Results are tied to a specific ARC-AGI-1 setup and controlled budget grid, so gains may not transfer directly to other datasets or unconstrained evaluation protocols.
paper_title: Pretraining and Test-Time Training Budgets Matter for ARC: A Controlled Study of VARC and TRM
